findings.title: VREFBUF obligation guards only against enabling the buffer; it omits the ENVR = 0 / HIZ = 0 mode, which pulls VREF+ (3V3A: VDDA, IMU and barometer supply) to VSSA

evidence.text: Keep VREFBUF_CSR at its reset value (ENVR = 0, HIZ = 1 per the ST SVD), never enable the buffer (no HAL_SYSCFG_EnableVREFBUF) ... an enabled buffer would drive its 1.5-2.5 V output ... against 3V3A

evidence.measured: U1.20 VREF+, U1.21 VDDA, U4.5 / U4.8 (ISM6HG256X VDDIO / VDD), U5.1 / U5.2 (MS5611), fed from 3V3 through R164 2.2 ohm

evidence.maker: STMicroelectronics RM0433 VREFBUF 'VREF buffer modes' table (as quoted on ST community for the STM32H753; RM0433 itself not re-read here: Inference)
evidence.text: ENVR = 0, HIZ = 0: VREFBUF buffer off, VREF+ pin pulled down to VSSA; ENVR = 0, HIZ = 1: external voltage reference mode (default); ENVR = 1, HIZ = 1: hold mode

evidence.page: Figure 95 p. 286 (VREF+ connected to VDDA); Table 189 p. 291

findings.impact: Documentation gap in a firmware obligation (no firmware exists; hardware unchanged). The obligation's stated hazard is ENVR = 1 only. HAL exposes HAL_SYSCFG_VREFBUF_HighImpedanceConfig(SYSCFG_VREFBUF_HIGH_IMPEDANCE_DISABLE), which clears HIZ with ENVR = 0; per the RM mode table that connects VREF+ to VSSA, i.e. loads 3V3A (behind 2.2 ohm) and so the IMU, barometer and ADC reference: loss of the roll-loop sensors. 'Keep at reset value' already forbids it implicitly, so the residual is a reader writing a HIZ-only call without seeing why.
findings.concrete_fix: Text only: in obligation 35 (r10_sch_check.py binding-note source, then regenerate) and docs/M3_R10.md Firmware add: 'Never clear HIZ either: ENVR = 0 with HIZ = 0 pulls VREF+ (3V3A: VDDA, U4, U5) to VSSA (RM0433 VREFBUF mode table; to be re-read: Inference). Do not call HAL_SYSCFG_VREFBUF_HighImpedanceConfig or write VREFBUF_CSR at all; bench check: 3V3A unchanged after VREFBUF clock enable.'

findings.title: Port endpoint level rule says 0-5 V, but at every battery power-up PORT_4V8 leads 3V3 by tens of ms, when the FT ceiling is 4.0 V; the spare AUX port invites an unspecified device

evidence.text: Direct port UARTs are FT digital inputs only, within 0 to 5 V
Their digital UARTs require powered-board FT setup, internal RX pulls always off and 0-5 V endpoints
configure FT digital RX with pulls disabled for any 5 V endpoint
PORT_4V8 can lead 3V3 by tens of ms because U11's 470 nF soft-start makes 3V3 lag (Inference); ... stay under the 4.0 V limit as long as the module's output high level is at most 3.6-4.0 V

evidence.page: Table 119 p. 212: FT VIN max = Min(VDD, VDDA, VDD33USB, VBAT) + 4.0 V, i.e. 4.0 V at VDD = 0; Table 120 note 3 p. 213: no positive injection on FT pins
Table 9-1 p. 13: 100 nF -> 780-800 V/s; C85 = 470 nF gives about 166-170 V/s, VLOGIC 0 -> 7.4 V in about 44 ms plus tSET (Calculation, inverse-C scaling)

evidence.reference: LOGIC_SS = {C85 470 nF, U11.11}; PORT_4V8 from RAW_PROTECTED via U400 (AP63201) and U401 (TPS7A9101, SS C408 10 nF) with no gating by 3V3
evidence.measured: RX pins PD9 (FT_h, Table 9 p. 75), PB12 (FT_u, p. 74), PC7 (FT_h, p. 79) see the module TX through 1 kohm only

evidence.text: a spare serial port for flight 2 without a respin

findings.impact: Bounded residual / documentation conflict. GPS and radio are 3.3 V LVTTL (per records), so the current defaults are within 4.0 V. A 5 V-logic device placed on any of J410 / J420 / J440 under the written 0-5 V rule would hold up to about 5 V on an FT pin with VDD = 0 for tens of ms at every power-up, beyond the absolute maximum (no clamp path; Table 119 note 4 also requires pulls off above 4 V). The records disagree with each other (VALIDATION 3.6-4.0 V vs obligation / ORDERING 0-5 V).
findings.concrete_fix: Text only: one rule in binding obligation 15 and 20, ORDERING 8.x (line 577 and the J410 / J420 / J440 rows), M3_R10 Firmware and REQUIREMENTS F10: 'Any device on J410, J420 or J440 must have a TX output high level <= 3.6 V (3.3 V LVTTL); 5 V-logic devices are not allowed on these ports, because PORT_4V8 is up for tens of ms before 3V3 at every power-up and the FT limit is then 4.0 V (DS12110 Rev 8 Table 119 p. 212).' Measure the PORT_4V8-to-3V3 lag on first articles.

findings.title: No obligation for a port with no mapped device (J440 by default, normally unplugged): its RX pin floats as a digital AF input if the UART is enabled

evidence.text: [2] default ... J440 AUX spare (USART6); [20] PD9/PB12/PC7 are digital AF inputs with internal pulls always disabled; [26] covers only no-net pins; [31] 'Direct port UARTs ... can float/noise when unplugged ... disable the affected UART after a bounded error threshold'

evidence.measured: no pull resistor on either side; J440.4 open when nothing is wired

evidence.page: Table 122 note 3 p. 215 / Table 157 note 7 p. 247 (pull rules); floating CMOS input current not specified (Inference)

findings.impact: Bounded residual (no hazard): an enabled USART6 on an open J440 sees a floating RX through 1 kohm and an unterminated stub, giving framing / noise interrupts and extra input-buffer current; obligation 31 only reacts after errors. The same applies to any port whose device is unplugged, and to the RX pins while PA4 is high (modules unpowered), which obligation 20 does not park (only TX pins).
findings.concrete_fix: Text only (binding obligation 2 / 20 and M3_R10 Firmware): 'A port with no device in the map (J440 by default) keeps both its pins in analog mode with its UART clock off; while PA4 is high, park the RX pins (PD9, PB12, PC7) analog too and stop the UARTs.'
